solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gourmet's dog tucking into last of nice pastry dish

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word nice is wanted
the dog is tucked inside the letters that follow, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A food lover's dog has its nose in a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gourmet's' is 'Gourmet is': the definition plus a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a gourmet is a connoisseur of fine food and drink.

clue.text: Slightly leavened bread: it feeds a social group at school

indicators.note: the word it is fed into the middle of the school group's letters

parts.note: the PTA, Parent-Teacher Association, is a school's social and fundraising body
taken as written

explanation.surface: Flatbread is supplied to a school's social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread that rises only a little.

clue.text: To some extent, teacher is hard to hold dear

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A teacher finds it difficult, up to a point, to be fond of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to treasure or love something is to hold it dear.

clue.text: Aussie native king banished from castle?

indicators.note: the king is thrown out of the chess piece's letters

parts.note: in chess the castle is also called a rook
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is exiled from his fortress, perhaps an Australian one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castle?' looks like a building; it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Short form: a roo is Australian slang for a kangaroo, native to that country.

clue.text: Put up with verbal abuse

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates being insulted.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: both senses are British colloquial, 'stick' meaning tolerate and 'get stick' meaning be criticised.

clue.text: Roofing contractor depositing pounds in bank?

indicators.note: the pounds are put inside the bank, as money is lodged

parts.note: a bank of seats is a tier, one row above another
L is short for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A builder pays money into his bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank?' suggests money; it is a tier, a raised row.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a tradesman who lays tiles on roofs.

clue.text: Drawing of box with ring in it

indicators.note: the ring goes inside the box, 'it' standing for the box

parts.note: a carton is a cardboard box
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A sketch of a jewellery box with a ring inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cartoon is a kind of drawing, often humorous.

clue.text: Abstemious type stocktaking in golfing store?

definitions.meaning: a person counting up the tees in a golf shop, a totaller of tees

explanation.surface: A sober person counts the stock in a golf shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a total abstainer from alcohol is abstemious.

clue.text: Sailors, swindled, so to speak, do a runner

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; ABS is the plural

indicators.note: the swindled word is said aloud, its spoken form spelt differently

parts.note: conned means swindled

explanation.surface: Cheated sailors run off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' signals that CONNED is to be spoken, giving COND.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'do a runner' is British slang for running away secretly, especially without paying.

clue.text: Vehicle initially transporting a football team, perhaps

indicators.note: only the first letter of transporting is used

parts.note: a football side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A vehicle carries a football side to a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a taxi is a hired vehicle for passengers.

clue.text: Problem about hot space for edible fungus

indicators.note: turned about, so the word for problem is written backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
room means space

explanation.surface: A puzzle concerning a heated area.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the field mushroom is a common edible fungus.

clue.text: Reportedly collected condiment

indicators.note: as spoken, the word for collected is heard rather than seen

parts.note: mustered means gathered or collected, as troops are

explanation.surface: A sauce said to be gathered together.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: mustard is a hot yellow condiment made from seeds.

clue.text: Ways to get round old feeling of pity

indicators.note: the ways go around the letter for old

parts.note: paths are ways

explanation.surface: Finding routes past an old feeling of compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: pathos is a quality evoking sorrow and compassion.

clue.text: American — one with capacity to be good-natured

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
able means having the capacity to do something

explanation.surface: A capable American who is kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: amiable means friendly and pleasant.

clue.text: Figure of old boy standing by pine?

indicators.note: one piece stands beside the other, placed next to it

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
to pine is to long for something

explanation.surface: A former pupil's form standing next to a pine tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine?' looks like a tree; it is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an oblong is a rectangle, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Recreation is taken in the French river

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the other letters

parts.note: le is French for the
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Pastime on a river in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: leisure is free time used for recreation.

clue.text: Sadly his dream is incorrectly taken in

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters going wrong, rearranged

explanation.surface: Unhappily, a man's dream is misunderstood.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphrase: something heard wrongly has been taken in incorrectly by the ear.

clue.text: Times? Sounds like yours and mine

indicators.note: the phrase is heard aloud, with the H silent

parts.note: ours means belonging to you and me

explanation.surface: A query about times, and a play on possessive pronouns.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun: hours are periods or times, as in 'opening hours'.

clue.text: Island's trendy church

parts.note: in means fashionable

explanation.surface: An island has a fashionable church.
explanation.definitionFit: Scottish word: an inch is a small island, as in Inchcolm in the Firth of Forth.

clue.text: Actors taking English class

indicators.note: the actors take on the extra letter, adding it

parts.note: the cast is the actors in a play

explanation.surface: Performers enrol in an English lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' looks like a lesson; it means social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a caste is a hereditary social class, especially in India.

clue.text: Musket son brought into passenger vehicle by mistake

indicators.note: beside, putting one piece next to the other

parts.note: a blunder is a mistake

indicators.note: the son is put inside the vehicle

parts.note: a bus carries passengers

explanation.surface: A firearm is accidentally carried onto a bus by a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by mistake' reads as 'accidentally'; it places BLUNDER beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a blunderbuss is a short, wide-muzzled old musket.

clue.text: Take to river, provoking argument?

definitions.meaning: to propel a boat with oars
a quarrel, the word said to rhyme with cow

explanation.surface: Taking to the water sparks a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Two words spelt alike: one means rowing a boat, the other a noisy quarrel.

clue.text: Like Lloyd George, say, mostly fit and quiet

indicators.note: most of the word, its final letter dropped

parts.note: well means healthy or fit
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A description of a former prime minister as mostly healthy and silent.
explanation.walkthrough: David Lloyd George, British prime minister 1916-22, was from Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Lloyd George was a famous man from Wales.

clue.text: Son given small number to soften up

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A boy is given a small figure to make him more agreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make someone more amenable is to soften them up.
